clue.text: Give way over cereal

parts.note: to sag is to give way or droop under weight
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone's breakfast collapses: give way over cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy grain-like food from palm pith, loosely counted among cereals and used in puddings.

clue.text: Hannibal's introduction into European battle, nothing less?

definitions.text: Hannibal's introduction into European battle, nothing less?

indicators.note: into says that opening letter is set inside the European battle
less says the word for nothing is dropped from the battle

parts.note: Lepanto was the 1571 naval battle between the Holy League and the Ottomans
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of Hannibal is wanted

explanation.surface: Hannibal brought something novel into a European war, nothing less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' drops O from LEPANTO, leaving LEPANT; 'into' then places H among E and LEPANT. The whole clue also describes the beast Hannibal famously led over the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannibal's most famous innovation in his Italian campaign was marching war beasts across the Alps, the very animal named here.

clue.text: Incompetent work on piano — tricky getting round that

indicators.note: getting round says the tricky word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a sly person is tricky or cunning

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it, so the work comes first

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A clumsy piano composition, with a tricky passage to get round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is careless and slapdash, the mark of someone lacking competence.

clue.text: Main role in ballet is lover I neglected

indicators.note: neglected says the letter I is left out of the lover

parts.note: a swain is an old poetic word for a young male lover

explanation.surface: A dancer's complaint: the lead in the ballet is a lover, and I've been neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: In Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake the lead ballerina dances Odette, the swan princess, the ballet's central role.

clue.text: Becoming mostly bitter, tucking into a lot of beef

indicators.note: tucking into says the shortened bitter word sits inside the shortened complaint
a lot of means not quite all, so the final letter of the complaint goes

parts.note: a beef is a complaint, as is a grouse

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the bitter word is dropped

parts.note: acid means bitter or sour

explanation.surface: A sour diner, mostly bitter, tucking into a large helping of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' is a complaint here, not meat; 'Becoming' is the adjective meaning seemly. Trimmed, the pieces are GROUS and ACI.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming as an adjective means fitting or graceful, and gracious behaviour is courteous and seemly in just that way.

clue.text: Plant account penned by American spies

indicators.note: penned by means written by, so the account is followed by its authors

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, its spies

explanation.surface: A report written up by American intelligence agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of trees and shrubs, the wattles and thorn trees, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Make useless vain flapping over Liberal, I see

indicators.note: in a down clue the scrambled piece sits over, above, the rest
flapping suggests agitated movement, so the letters of vain are scrambled

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics
to see someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A flustered politician fusses over a Liberal colleague and declares it pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' rearranges VAIN to INVA; 'over' places it above the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To invalidate something is to render it void or ineffective, depriving it of any use.

clue.text: No dancer recalled mistake about line further down

indicators.note: about says the turned word goes around the line
recalled is read as called back, so the mistake is turned round

parts.note: a flaw is a mistake or defect
lower means further down

explanation.surface: A dancer misremembers a step, a slip about a line further down the routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns FLAW into WALF, and 'about' sets L inside it to make WALLF.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is the shy person left at the edge of a dance without a partner, so not dancing.

clue.text: Type of sugar not popular for tooth

indicators.note: not says the popular word is taken away from the tooth

parts.note: a canine is a pointed tooth
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A kind of sugar that is unpopular with dentists, being bad for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cane sugar is refined from sugar cane, one of the two main commercial sources of sugar.

clue.text: Developer very much ahead

parts.note: so means very much, as in so tired
up means ahead, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A property developer far ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is old photographers' slang for the developing solution in which film is processed in a darkroom.

clue.text: Article in photo producing alarm

indicators.note: in says the article is placed inside the photo

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article in which a photograph causes alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, the same sense as alarm in a frightened rush.

clue.text: Sandbank about to return and drift sideways

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: a bar is a sandbank across a river mouth
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A boat near a sandbank turns back and drifts sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: To crab is to move sideways, as a crab walks, a term used of boats and aircraft blown off course.

clue.text: Grant, perhaps, to import a new sweet wine

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the other letters go inside the actor's name

parts.note: Cary Grant was the Hollywood film star; perhaps marks a first name given by example

explanation.surface: A merchant named Grant arranges to import a new dessert wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary was a sweet fortified wine from the Canary Islands, popular in Shakespeare's day as sack.

clue.text: Dreadful delay involving Queen worried sufficiently

indicators.note: involving says the scrambled word wraps around the other pieces
dreadful suggests something awful has happened to the letters, so delay is scrambled

parts.note: ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A dreadful delay leaves the Queen worried, but things get done well enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges the fodder to ADELY, which then takes the other pieces into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequately means well enough to meet the need, which is what sufficiently says.

clue.text: Detectives are ditching English operations, backtracking on an irregular basis

indicators.note: backtracking says the whole string is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

indicators.note: ditching means discarding, so the E goes from are

parts.note: OPS is the usual short form of operations

explanation.surface: Detectives drop an English operation and retreat from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' turns ARE into AR; CID, AR and OPS give CIDAROPS, which 'backtracking' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sporadic occurs only now and then, at scattered intervals rather than regularly.

clue.text: Head of serpent mostly emulating Adam and Eve in Eden? Wily thing

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
mostly says the final letter of that word is dropped

parts.words: emulating Adam and Eve in Eden
parts.note: before the Fall, Adam and Eve went about naked in the garden

explanation.surface: The serpent of Genesis, the wily tempter, comparing itself with the naked pair in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The snake is proverbially sly and cunning, from the serpent who tempted Eve onward.

clue.text: Immoral gamble absorbing number

indicators.note: absorbing says the gamble takes the number inside it

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

explanation.surface: A shady gamble that soaks up a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is British slang for corrupt or dishonest, as in a bent copper.

clue.text: Informer comprehends losing power

indicators.note: losing says the P is dropped from the word

parts.note: grasps means understands or comprehends
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An informer who understands things but has lost his influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is British slang for a police informer, from rhyming slang grasshopper, copper.

clue.text: Hard work removing new bit of hair in jam

indicators.note: removing says the N is taken out of the word

parts.note: a grind is tedious hard work
a lock is a tress, a bit of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's hard slog, removing a new strand caught in a tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gridlock is total traffic congestion, a jam in which nothing moves.

clue.text: Opening without latest lead actor

indicators.note: the latest letter is the last one, so the final T is removed

parts.note: a start is an opening or beginning

explanation.surface: A play's opening night goes ahead without the newest leading man.
explanation.definitionFit: The star is the principal performer, the headline name in a play or film.

clue.text: Possibly overlooked source of smoke — burning?

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: lighted means set alight, burning

explanation.surface: Something overlooked might be where the smoke is coming from, still alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slighted is to be snubbed or treated as unimportant, one way of being overlooked; possibly marks that loose fit.

clue.text: A lot of point in blocking attractive bargain

indicators.note: blocking says the shortened point sits inside the attractive word, blocking it

parts.note: cute means attractive

indicators.note: a lot of means most of, so the last letter of prick goes

parts.note: a prick is a sharp point, as of a thorn

explanation.surface: A sharp point blocks something pretty in a cheap sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' keeps all but the last letter of the point, giving PRIC; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-price goods are sold at a reduced price, so a cut-price item is a bargain.

clue.text: Quantity of energy given by a component of salad?

parts.note: pep means vigour or energy
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: How much energy a salad ingredient supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet pepper, red or green, is often sliced into a salad; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Peevishly complain French article about wine is regressive

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
vin is French for wine
is shortened to 's as in it's

explanation.surface: A French piece about wine is backward-looking, enough to make readers grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: LE, VIN and S give LEVINS, which 'regressive' reverses; 'about' is a link meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to whine and grumble tearfully, a peevish way of complaining.

clue.text: No restricting one in series from an older time

indicators.note: in says that combination goes inside the series
restricting says the word No hems the one in

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: No single episode in the series dates from an earlier era.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior means older or of an earlier generation, as father is senior to son.

clue.text: No repetition in expensive part of programme

indicators.note: the word has a doubled letter, and no repetition means one copy is dropped

parts.note: steep means expensive, as in steep prices

explanation.surface: An expensive step in a programme is not to be repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stage in a process or programme of action.

clue.text: Revolutionary piano melodies bearing fruit

indicators.note: Revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
bearing means carrying, so the words hold the answer's letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Radical piano tunes start paying off.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'bearing fruit' as the definition, but 'bearing' is the signal that the letters are carried inside 'piano melodies'; 'Revolutionary' turns NOMEL round.
explanation.definitionFit: The lemon is a sour yellow citrus, an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Some cloth to munch? That'll show me up

definitions.text: Some cloth to munch? That'll show me up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the found letters read from bottom to top
some says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: An insect finds cloth to eat and boasts it will embarrass its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds HTOM across 'cloth to munch', and 'show me up' reverses it. Read whole, the clue is the insect itself, revealed by holes in clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes moth larvae eat wool and other cloth, and the holes they leave betray them.

clue.text: Hot gas is subject of clip

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps
air is a mixture of gases, loosely a gas

explanation.surface: Hot gas is the topic of a news clip.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut clips hair, so hair is what clippers work on.

clue.text: Injured lady heartlessly, without much thought

indicators.note: without their hearts, both words keep only their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman hurt by someone acting carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' looks like an anagram signal, but it is fodder: 'heartlessly' strips the middles from both 'Injured' and 'lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something idly means doing it casually and lazily, without real thought or purpose.

clue.text: University lecturer recalled in live university award

indicators.note: in says the turned letters go inside the word for live

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the two letters are turned round

explanation.surface: A lecturer called back to a university to receive an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge a Blue is awarded to someone who represents the university in a sport.

clue.text: Insect repellent dispersed into cellar

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are spread out anew

explanation.surface: Bug spray is sprayed into the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Citronella oil, from a lemon-scented grass, is widely used in candles and sprays to keep mosquitoes away.
